findings.reason: I confirmed that deleteCacheMutation never invalidates connectedCalendars, that EventAdvancedTab renders the wrapper with no onChanged, and that the query sets refetchOnWindowFocus:false, so on that tab the old cache status stays on screen after a delete until the page reloads.

I confirmed that the Alert branch used to check only delegationCredentialId, while it now also passes disableConnectionModification, which EventAdvancedTab sets to true, so on that tab a broken credential no longer has a remove action.

It is true that nothing reads SelectedCalendar.updatedAt or googleChannelId (the UI uses CalendarCache.updatedAt), so the write looks unused, but whether Prisma skips an empty updateMany is uncertain and the finding is framed as a question.
The handler does throw a plain Error, which tRPC reports as INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR rather than NOT_FOUND; this is a minor status-code and error-reporting issue only.
The timestamp is formatted with a hardcoded 'en-US' locale inside a translated string; this is a real but small i18n inconsistency.
The dev helper script does use the BSD-only `sed -i ''` form and an ENV_FILE path relative to the current directory; both are valid points about a local tooling script, not product code.
DEFAULT NOW() does stamp existing rows with the deploy time, so the UI's 'Last updated' will be misleading for them, and the header comment is stale; the impact is minor and temporary.
